versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# EHS-201 Injury reporting and recordkeeping (Ohio, federal OSHA)

- Every injury is reported the same shift. No one is discouraged from reporting, and no incentive depends on
  injury-free days (29 CFR 1904.35).
- Recordability is decided by the EHS coordinator from the facts (29 CFR 1904.7): medical treatment beyond first
  aid (including a prescription, or non-prescription medicine at prescription strength), days away, restricted
  work, or a diagnosed significant injury. An elastic wrap, ice or a non-prescription dose is first aid.
- Enter recordable cases on the 300 log and the 301 within 7 calendar days of learning of them (1904.29). Agency
  associates we supervise day to day go on our log (1904.31).
- Powered industrial trucks: an operator involved in an accident or near miss is retrained and re-evaluated
  before operating again (1910.178(l)(4)).
- The EHS Director (Carmen Vidal) reviews every recordable and every near miss involving a forklift.

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# HR-110 Attendance, leave and pay

- Workweek: Sunday 00:00 to Saturday 23:59. Overtime is 1.5x for hours over 40 in that workweek; hours are never
  averaged across weeks, and unapproved overtime is still paid.
- Attendance points don't apply to absences that may be protected leave. If an absence may be for a serious
  health condition of the associate or a family member, the supervisor tells HR the same day; HR sends the FMLA
  notice within five business days.
- Associates may take reasonable time to vote on Election Day without penalty (Ohio R.C. 3599.06).

versions.content:
# OPS-310 Value-added services (kitting, labeling, bagging) at the DCs

- Price per unit = (standard labor hours per unit x $33.50 loaded labor rate + materials at cost) x 1.20.
- The site lead sets VAS prices by this formula (rounded to the cent) and gives them to the account manager in
  writing. A price below the formula, or a VAS commitment over 200 labor hours a month at one site, needs the
  Regional VP.
- The labor standard comes from a timed study of at least 10 cycles (Inventory Control), or the LMS standard
  where one exists.
- Quotes are valid 90 days.

documents.title: EHS-204 Powered industrial trucks (forklifts, reach trucks, order pickers, powered pallet jacks)

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# EHS-204 Powered industrial trucks

- Authorization is by truck type. An operator drives only the types listed on a current evaluation; each type is
  evaluated at least every three years (29 CFR 1910.178(l)(4)(iii)) and after any near miss, accident or unsafe
  operation (refresher first). The EHS tracker is the record.
- Every truck is inspected with the pre-shift checklist before use on each shift (1910.178(q)(7)). A truck with a
  defect that affects safe operation is tagged out and stays out of service until repaired (1910.178(q)(1)); no
  one may override a tag except maintenance after the repair.
- No one under 18 operates any powered truck, including powered pallet jacks (federal law prohibits forklifts and
  other high-lift trucks for 16-17 year olds, 29 CFR 570.58; Calder extends it to every powered truck). Agencies
  confirm age at placement.
- Agency operators we supervise follow the same rules.
